name: The Hated
label: Simple Machines
lede: Two St. John's College kids in Annapolis, a name dreamed up on a kibbutz, five years of church basements, and a reunion 35 years later.

eras.title: A band named on a kibbutz
eras.text: Two St. John's College kids, Erik Fisher and Daniel Littleton, turn Beatles covers and a name dreamed up abroad into an Annapolis hardcore band, 30 miles from the Washington scene that inspired it.

years.h: Erik Fisher and Daniel Littleton start the band
years.p: Childhood friends whose fathers taught at St. John's College, Fisher and Littleton begin with The Dead Beatles, playing faster, distorted Beatles songs. Fisher had come up with the name The Hated during a stay on a kibbutz in Israel.
years.xp:
According to Tone Glow, Fisher pictured the name on an American flag and sent it to Littleton by letter. The pair grew up in a house of musical parents and traded long talks about philosophy and music.

Wikipedia lists MDC, the Minutemen and Annapolis's Spastic Rats among their early touchstones. Before The Hated they had played in short-lived groups such as Fit of Rage and Geek Patrol, according to Andrew Gebhardt.

years.h: Church basements and a Foucault pendulum room
years.p: The Hated play wherever Annapolis will have them: church basements, an elementary school playground and the pendulum chamber at St. John's College.
years.xp: Fisher also ran a zine, CRAB, short for Citizens for the Reeducation of the Annapolis Bourgeoisie, covering local bands and politics. Tone Glow and Gebhardt both describe a scene held together by the Annapolis Record Exchange and Kenny Hill's Vermin Scum label.

years.h: Debut tape: The Best Piece of Shit Vol. 3
years.p: The Hated release their first recording themselves, with Fisher on vocals and guitar, Littleton on bass, Colin Meeder on guitar and Mike Bonner on drums.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates it to 1985 and lists it as self-released. Decades later Numero Group's Ken Shipley and Littleton dug up more from this period for a Vol. 4.

eras.title: Vermin Scum and a new drummer
eras.text: Kenny Hill, the drummer of the Spastic Rats and founder of Vermin Scum, first releases the band and then takes over the drum stool.

years.p: The first Hated record on Kenny Hill's Vermin Scum label, cut at LSP Studios in Annapolis.
years.xp: LSP was an 8-track studio in Les Lentz's parents' house in Hillsmere, per Gebhardt, and documented bands including Spastic Rats and Moss Icon.

years.h: Kenny Hill replaces Mike Bonner on drums
years.p: Hill, of the Spastic Rats and boss of Vermin Scum, joins the band he had been releasing.
A second release, put out by the band itself, in the middle of the run of tapes and 7-inches.
The band's second Vermin Scum record, the last before Fisher's return to college slowed things down.

eras.title: Every Song, and a last show in Crofton
eras.text: Fisher goes back to school, the band records what will be its final album, and the original Hated ends in Maryland.

years.p: The final studio album of the original band, made as Erik Fisher resumed his college studies.
The original Hated play their final gig in Crofton, ending a five-year run.
years.xp: Littleton went on to form Ida with Elizabeth Mitchell. Wikipedia gives no more detail on the Crofton show.

eras.title: Awl on the Tool Cassette Series
eras.text: Simple Machines gathers the band's scattered 1985 to 1988 recordings on tape, on a cassette for the label's Tool series.

years.p: Sixteen tracks, mostly recorded at LSP Studios between summer 1985 and winter 1987-88, on Simple Machines.
years.xp: Discogs lists Meeder and John Irvine sharing bass duties and Bonner and Hill both on drums. One Discogs reviewer says some copies were badly dubbed, which cut off the starts of songs.

eras.title: Kenny Hill's death and the archive
eras.text: Littleton builds Ida, and the band's old tapes eventually find a bigger audience.

years.p: Hill, who founded Vermin Scum and played drums in the band from 1985, died in Brooklyn Park, Maryland, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: Numero digs it up, the band returns
eras.text: The Numero Group reissues the Hated's archive and reunites the band on stage for the first time in about 35 years.

years.h: The Best Piece of Shit, Vol. 4, Numero Group
years.p: Ken Shipley and Daniel Littleton assemble unreleased early Hated material for Numero.

years.h: The Hated play again after about 35 years
years.p: Fisher, Littleton, Meeder, Bonner, John Irvine, Miggy Littleton and Jason Fisher reunite, playing Numero Twenty and a home-town show.
years.xp: Tone Glow dates the reunion to January 15, 2023, with shows in January and February. Wikipedia says the return was for Numero Group's Numero Twenty festival.

years.p: A second Numero collection of Hated recordings.
